Getting an API key for OpenAI or Claude

Source: vignettes/articles/api-keys.Rmd
api-keys.Rmd

To generate synthetic respondents with OpenAI or Anthropic (Claude) models, synthcheck needs an API key: A long secret text that tells the provider who is calling and whose account pays for the calls. This article walks through getting one from each provider, adding credit, keeping the key private and capping what you can spend. It takes about ten minutes per provider.

You do not need a key to try synthcheck. The Mock provider gives random answers for free, the built-in hexaco_llm holds answers from six models, and Ollama runs open models on your own computer at no cost. See the app demos for runs without a key.

Before you start

  • The API is separate from the chat apps. A ChatGPT Plus or a Claude Pro or Max subscription does not include API use. The API has its own account page, its own billing and pay-as-you-go prices.
  • You pay per call. Each synthetic respondent is one call (one per block of items when an instrument is split). The price depends on the model and the length of the prompt and the answer. synthcheck’s default models are the cheapest of each provider, and the app shows the estimated cost before every paid run.
  • Start with a small credit. A few dollars are enough to try a real model on a short scale. Add more once you know what a full run costs.

The provider pages below change from time to time, so a button may have a slightly different name. The steps stay the same.

OpenAI

  1. Sign up. Go to openai.com/api and choose to sign up or log in. This opens the OpenAI platform (platform.openai.com), which is the API side of OpenAI. You can use the same login as ChatGPT.
  2. Add credit. Open Settings, then Billing, add a payment method and buy credit. OpenAI uses prepaid credit: Calls stop when the credit runs out, unless you switch on automatic recharge. Leave automatic recharge off at first.
  3. Create a key. Open the API keys page (platform.openai.com/api-keys), click Create new secret key, give it a name such as synthcheck, and copy it. The key starts with sk-. OpenAI shows it only once: If you lose it, delete it and create a new one.
  4. Set a limit. Under Settings, the Limits page (and the budget of each project) lets you set a monthly budget and an email alert. A small budget is a good guard against a run that is larger than you meant.

Claude (Anthropic)

  1. Sign up. Go to the Claude Console at platform.claude.com/dashboard and create an account. The Console is the API side of Anthropic. It is separate from the Claude chat app, though you can sign in with the same email.
  2. Add credit. Open Settings, then Billing (platform.claude.com/settings/billing), and click Buy credits. Calls stop when the credit runs out, unless you switch on auto-reload. Leave auto-reload off at first.
  3. Create a key. Open Settings, then API keys, click Create key, name it synthcheck and copy it. The key starts with sk-ant-. The Console shows it only once.
  4. Set a limit. The Limits page under Settings shows the spend limit of your account, and lets you set a lower monthly limit of your own.

Using the key in synthcheck

There are two ways to give synthcheck the key.

In the app. Paste the key into Anthropic API key or OpenAI API key on the Models tab. A typed key stays in memory for that session only. It is never written to the saved data, the run settings, the report or the R script, so you paste it again the next time you open the app.

In .Renviron (recommended). Save the key once, and both the app and your R code find it without showing it. Open the file with

usethis::edit_r_environ()   # or file.edit("~/.Renviron")

add one line per provider, and restart R:

OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

The app then says that it found the key, and sc_model("openai") and sc_model("anthropic") use it in code. Check that R sees it with nzchar(Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")), which should be TRUE.

Before the first real run, start small: One attempt and two respondents per persona. In the app, Estimate run time sends one test call per model, which checks that the key and the model id work. In code, estimate_cost() shows what a run is likely to cost:

ins <- sc_builtin_instrument("rses")
estimate_cost(ins, list(sc_model("anthropic"), sc_model("openai")),
              attempts = 1, respondents = 20)

Every answer is kept in synthcheck’s response cache, so running the same settings again costs nothing (see the response cache).

Keeping the key private

An API key works like a password that can spend your money.

  • Do not share it. Do not paste it into emails, chats, shared documents or screenshots.
  • Keep it out of code and Git. Do not write it into an R script, an R Markdown file or a Shiny app. .Renviron in your home folder is outside your projects. If you keep a project-level .Renviron, add it to .gitignore.
  • Run the app on your own computer. Do not deploy the app with a typed key on a shared server.
  • One key per use. A separate key named synthcheck can be deleted without breaking anything else.
  • If a key leaks, delete it. Delete it on the provider’s API keys page straight away and create a new one. Then check the usage page for calls you did not make.

If something goes wrong

  • “Invalid API key” or 401: The key was copied with a missing character or a space, or it was deleted. Create a new one.
  • “Insufficient credit”, “quota” or 429 right away: The account has no credit yet, or the budget is reached. Add credit or raise the limit. A new account can take a few minutes before the first paid call goes through.
  • 429 during a run: The provider is limiting how many calls you make at once. Lower Calls at the same time on the Models tab (parallel in generate_synthetic()).
  • The app does not see the key from .Renviron: Restart R after you edit the file, and start the app again.
